A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MP-HSIR paper, including all 21 pages and supplementary Sections F–J. Text, equations, tables, and figure resources match apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original restoration experiments, generalization tests, real-world evaluations, and ablations in Section 4, with further experimental results in the supplementary material.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the same original restoration, generalization, real-world, and ablation results in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

M1.justification: The MP-HSIR architecture, spectral and text-visual prompts, degradation predictor, training objectives, and restoration procedures are identical.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 13 datasets, seven jointly trained restoration tasks, motion-deblurring and Poisson-denoising generalization tests, real-world evaluations, and composite-degradation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including AirNet, PromptIR, PIP, HAIR, InstructIR, PromptHSI, and the same task-specific methods.

E3.justification: Reported dataset partitions, degradation settings, evaluation metrics, model widths, training budgets, and few-shot/zero-shot protocols are identical in Section 4.1 and the supplementary material.

E4.justification: Module ablations in Tables 3 and 16–18, spectral and prompt analyses, efficiency comparisons, and controllable/sequential restoration cases are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate and averaging practices. Neither reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results match throughout both PDFs and their appendices. For example, Table 2 retains MP-HSIR's motion-deblurring PSNR/SSIM of 40.06/0.965 and Poisson-denoising values of 38.56/0.922.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and their mathematical definitions and reasoning are identical. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about universal multi-prompt restoration, spectral recovery, controllability, and performance across nine tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning spectral-prompt robustness, degradation discrimination, generalization, and controllability are unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, dataset processing, predictor training details, and the code/model access link are identical. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 81 references are unchanged, preserving the same positioning relative to prior restoration and prompt-based methods.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2, 11 Jul 2025 to v3, 28 Dec 2025, with its self-link updated accordingly. The title, authors, prose, section order, and supplementary organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–15 and Tables 1–18 retain identical content, captions, styling, and placement. The body and supplementary layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, methods, experiments, results, and appendices are identical. Updating only the administrative arXiv version/date stamp and self-link produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
